text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Ida B. Wells was born enslaved on July 16, 1862, in Holly Springs, Mississippi, during the Civil War. [D]

In the yellow fever epidemic of 1878, when she was 16, both her parents and an infant brother died; she left school and took on the care of her surviving younger siblings, teaching to support them. [D]

She was an investigative journalist and editor who documented lynching in the United States, notably in A Red Record (1895), and campaigned against it for the rest of her life; she was also a suffragist and civil rights leader. [D]
On June 27, 1895, she married the Chicago attorney Ferdinand L. Barnett, kept her own name alongside his, and settled in Chicago; they had four children. [D]

She signed the call for the 1909 conference that led to the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People and is considered one of its founders, though she was left off the list of its founding committee and later drew away from it. [D]
In 1930 she ran, unsuccessfully, for the Illinois State Senate. [D]

She began writing her autobiography in her last years; it was published after her death as Crusade for Justice: The Autobiography of Ida B. Wells, edited by her youngest daughter, Alfreda M. Duster. [D]

list.item: Tiredness for some months and ankle swelling by evening, with a raised creatinine (1.42 mg/dL, race-free eGFR 40, confirmed at 38 with cystatin C) and albumin in the urine (240 mg/g) found today; cause and chronicity to be established: active, confirmed [S]
Elevated blood pressure at intake (164/94 mmHg, average of two readings), without a diagnosis of hypertension; home readings for one week to confirm: active, confirmed [S]

Nephrology consultation for reduced kidney function (race-free eGFR 38) with albuminuria of uncertain cause, a 5-year kidney failure risk above 5% if the disease proves chronic, and APOL1 genetic counseling. Guideline: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, anemia and depression monographs (2026) [S]

Confirm and stage the kidney disease: race-free eGFR from creatinine with cystatin C, repeat urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, urinalysis with microscopy, kidney ultrasound, a monoclonal protein screen (serum protein electrophoresis and free light chains), hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests, and any earlier results she can obtain. Guideline: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024); A Unifying Approach for GFR Estimation: Recommendations of the NKF-ASN Task Force on Reassessing the Inclusion of Race in Diagnosing Kidney Disease (2021); New Creatinine- and Cystatin C-Based Equations to Estimate GFR without Race (2021) [S]

Blood pressure: a validated home monitor with readings twice a day for seven days to confirm the diagnosis; sodium below 2 g a day; recheck in two weeks. Guideline: KDIGO 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Blood Pressure in Chronic Kidney Disease (2021); 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, anemia and depression monographs (2026) [S]

Stop over-the-counter naproxen and use acetaminophen for knee aching; avoid all NSAIDs; tell every clinician and pharmacist about her kidneys before new medicines or contrast dye. Guideline: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, anemia and depression monographs (2026) [S]

Anemia and mineral and bone checks: hemoglobin with iron studies, calcium, phosphate, intact PTH and 25-hydroxyvitamin D at baseline. Guideline: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024); Executive summary of the 2017 KDIGO Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral and Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD) Guideline Update (2017); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, anemia and depression monographs (2026) [S]

Baseline ECG, TSH for tiredness, a lipid panel once at diagnosis, A1c to screen for diabetes, and a PHQ-9. Guideline: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, anemia and depression monographs (2026); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]
